v0.1.8 is available

Download v0.1.8 for Windows, Linux or macOS. This stable software release is an early-alpha simulator; aircraft and ground-vehicle models remain experimental.

Independent evaluation of some experimental aircraft remains open:

  • The Stik’s 240 Hz sideslip-limit check remains open; it is an estimated boundary check.
  • The R02 yaw-damping comparison remains open; its model comparison is not a physical measurement.

ANATOMY OF THE SIMULATION

From a movement of the stick
to the response of the aircraft.

Explore the systems already in the source. Each area links to its documentation and current limits.

INPUT→240 Hz→FLIGHT
01

Aerodynamics and flight dynamics

+

A custom six-degree-of-freedom solver with RK4 integration at 240 Hz and float64 state. Local wing and tail loads, trim, stalls, spins and control-surface dynamics.

  • Downwash, pitch damping and propeller wake where configured.
  • Optional wing and tail ground effect, declared for the Stik.
  • A dedicated helicopter session for the fuselage, rotor, rotor inflow and controls.
Simulator architecture ↗
02

Four ways to make power

+

Two- and four-stroke glow engines, gasoline, electric propulsion and a spooling turbine. Torque, gyroscopic effects, P-factor and propwash depend on each aircraft’s modules.

  • Experimental glow installations: finite fuel, mixture and tank feed.
  • Coupled motor, ESC and battery models; LUMBER uses a prescribed 4S bus without depletion.
  • Estimated and borrowed parameters are documented as such.
Glow engines and limits ↗ Electric propulsion ↗
03

Flight starts on the ground, too

+

Individual wheel rotation, suspension, steering, rolling resistance and tire slip. Maintained grass and rough ground have different surface profiles.

  • Experimental runway starts for the Stik and LUMBER.
  • Skid contacts and ground-pad startup for the helicopter.
  • Simplified scenery collision models, wreckage, marks and effects; physical calibration remains open.
Ground contact model ↗
04

Air, light and flying conditions

+

Uniform wind, repeating gusts and seeded turbulence. Configurable elevation, temperature, QNH pressure and humidity for the physical atmosphere.

  • Dawn, day, dusk, night and passing evening; editable date, time and location.
  • Clouds, rain and lightning are visual effects; they do not apply spatially varying storm forces.
  • Field lights, stars, moonlight and the helicopter’s night kit.
Atmosphere ↗ Time and lighting ↗
05

Transmitters, instruments and practice

+

USB transmitter, gamepad and keyboard, with calibration, arming and failsafe. Aircraft-specific rates and expo for keyboard and gamepad; radios retain their own settings.

  • Pilot, chase, orbit and close-up cameras, with manual or automatic zoom.
  • Independent flight data, sticks, trims, wind, telemetry and diagnostic panels.
  • Aircraft Workshop variants, repeatable randomized conditions and optional emergency practice.
Controls and first flight ↗ Aircraft Workshop ↗
06

A field you can see and hear

+

Grass, trees, a lake, club buildings, vehicles, people and birds. Positional engine, propeller, wind, foliage and wildlife sound, with motion-dependent Doppler.

  • Glow exhaust and optional smoke drifting with the wind.
  • Impact effects, debris and visual damage persist until restart.
  • Water does not simulate buoyancy; in-flight aircraft structural failure is not implemented.
World and scenery ↗ Audio ↗
07

Sourced data. Repeatable flights.

+

The openrc-aircraft v2 contract requires units, evidence type and source. Invalid configurations cannot fly. Geometry and physical data are regenerated from their sources.

  • F10 records fixed-wing flights; F11 marks maneuvers. CSV export and comparisons use the same input tape.
  • Regression tests, golden flights, captures and export checks.
  • Software equivalence does not demonstrate physical realism: measurements and pilots are needed.
Aircraft data contract ↗ Flight logging and replay ↗

BEFORE YOUR FIRST FLIGHT

RC flight simulator:
your questions, answered.

Is OpenRC Simulator free?

Yes. OpenRC Simulator is free to download, and its source code is available under the MIT license. Aircraft, scenery and other assets retain their own licenses. You can inspect the code, report issues or contribute on GitHub.

How do I install it on Windows, Linux or macOS?

Download the ZIP for your operating system, extract it and launch the application. You do not need to install Godot. Compare the archive checksum with SHA256SUMS from the same release, and read the platform instructions and signing limitations in the first-launch guide. Choose your download.

Do I need an RC transmitter to fly?

No. You can use a keyboard or a gamepad. USB transmitters can be used as flight controls when the operating system detects them as a compatible joystick; axis setup and calibration may be required. Support is not guaranteed for every radio or adapter. See the controls and calibration guide.

Can I fly in the browser?

OpenRC is a desktop simulator. This website shows aircraft turntables and an optional 3D model viewer; these are previews, not playable flights. Download the desktop app to fly.

How realistic is the flight simulation?

OpenRC has its own flight solver and experimental aircraft models. Software tests and repeatable flight logs help detect regressions, but do not establish physical accuracy. Independent measurements and pilot evaluation remain necessary. Read the validation roadmap and the notes for the aircraft you choose.
